paper_metadata.title: The determining role of Al addition on tribology properties and oxidation behavior at elevated temperatures of TiZrHfNb refractory high-entropy alloy

evidence.quote: This study developed a series of Alx(TiZrHfNb)100-x (x = 0, 3, 5, 7, 12 at. %) refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) with an aim to improve the poor oxidation and wear resistance at elevated temperature of the base alloy TiZrHfNb.
TiZrHfNb with a single BCC phase

The Alx(TiZrHfNb)100-x (x = 0, 3, 5, 7, 12 at.%; donated as Al-0, Al-3%, Al-5%, Al-7% and Al-12%) alloys were prepared by arc-melting in water-cooled copper crucible under a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere.

The Alx(TiZrHfNb)100-x (x = 0, 3, 5, 7, 12 at.%; donated as Al-0, Al-3%, Al-5%, Al-7% and Al-12%) alloys were prepared by arc-melting in water-cooled copper crucible under a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere. To ensure chemical homogeneity, the RHEA ingots were overturned and re-melted at least five times and then cast into a water-cooled copper mold with dimensions of 60 × 20 × 6 mm3.
The alloys were then cold-rolled by an 80% reduction in thickness, and the final thickness was 1.7 – 1.9 mm.
A recrystallization annealing treatment was performed at 1000 ◦C for 30 min, and then quenched in water.

attributes.morphology: needle-shaped at interface, short rod-shaped in matrix
attributes.location: grain boundary and interface between oxygen-enriched layer and matrix

evidence.quote: The precipitates in the interface are needle-shaped, while the precipitates in matrix is short rod-shaped. The EDS analysis (Point ID) confirms that these precipitates are enriched in Zr and Al atoms. According to previous reports, it can be determined that the precipitates are Zr5Al3 [18,30].

attributes.location: outermost side of the oxide layer

evidence.quote: The Al atoms form a very thin(~5 μm) oxide layer on the outermost side of the oxide layer, which inhibits the further oxidation of the alloy, thereby improving the oxidation resistance of the alloy (Fig. 8 b).

in Al-12% alloy, the yield strength increases by 3.3 times, reaching up to 1094.8 MPa.

The addition of Al significantly improves the strength of the RHEAs due to the large solid solution strengthening effect
The increase of hardness can be attributed to the significant localized lattice distortion produced by the atomic size difference and then improve the solution hardening.

the Al element will preferentially react with O atoms and accumulate on the surface to form a dense oxide layer, which prevents other elements reacting with O atoms and makes the alloy have better oxidation resistance at high temperatures
